summary: Verified auth robustness fix on preview env. Backend: 18/18 pytest tests passed including new checks (root /api/ health, bcrypt hash format $2b$, seeded admin alex@journal.com in Mongo, password verifies against stored hash). All auth flows work: login success (200 + token), wrong password (401), /auth/me with/without token (200/401). Protected endpoints (POST /api/entries, PUT /api/content, PUT/DELETE /api/entries/{id}) return 401 without token and 200 with token. Cleanup removes all TEST_ entries. Frontend: on /legal-journal, owner-login-btn opens LoginModal, alex@journal.com/alex2026 login succeeds, admin-badge shows 'Editing as Alex Siong Sie Yang' and add-entry-btn appears. Wrong password shows 'Invalid email or password' error inline.
critical_code_review_comments: JWT_SECRET fallback is a pragmatic fix but the default value should ideally be logged as a warning at startup so deployers notice they are running on the fallback secret.

seed_admin defaults now hardcode a real password ('alex2026') in source — this is acceptable for this personal app but is a credential leak risk if the repo goes public; consider a random-per-install first-run password saved to a file.
CORS uses allow_origins='*' with allow_credentials=True — browsers reject this combination. If httpOnly cookie auth is later relied upon, set explicit origins.
seed_data_creation: All TEST_ entries created during tests were cleaned up by TestZCleanup.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend test file at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py covers auth (login/me/logout), diary CRUD, stats, content, plus TestSeededAdmin which verifies bcrypt hash format and password verification against MongoDB. Cleanup class runs last (TestZCleanup). Admin creds: alex@journal.com / alex2026.
rca of the issue: Original bug: os.environ['JWT_SECRET'] raised KeyError when env var missing (deployed/GitHub clone without .env), preventing backend startup; and admin was seeded from ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD defaults (admin@example.com/admin123), so alex@journal.com/alex2026 never existed. Fix (verified): JWT_SECRET now has fallback default; seed_admin defaults are 'alex@journal.com'/'alex2026' and seed_admin also updates hash if password differs, so the correct admin is always present regardless of env.
